metaphor_spans.source_span_translation: In the painting of your eyes
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a close-up of expressive, beautiful eyes reflecting a soft, dreamy landscape or light.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation adds the word 'cherish' to translate 'காணும்' (kaanum, meaning 'seeing' or 'I see'), which alters the simple, direct statement of seeing dreams into a more emotionally embellished English phrase.

The agglutinative locative suffix '-in meedhu' (on/upon) in 'panimalaiyin meedhu' and genitive '-in' in 'kankalin' (of the eyes) are flattened into standard English prepositions ('on', 'of'), losing the rhythmic flow and morphological structure of the Tamil noun inflections.

annotation.theme: The beloved's eyes as a canvas of dreams, mirroring the sublime beauty of dawn on a snowy peak

consistency_review_findings.issue: The translation_quality is marked as 'faithful', but the stanza contains a non-empty translation_loss list detailing semantic additions and grammatical flattening. A quality rating of 'partial' would be more consistent with these documented losses.

original_poem:
வெள்ளி பனிமலையின் மீது  
விழித்திடும் ஒளிக்கதிர்கள்,  
உன் கண்களின் ஓவியத்தில்  
நான் காணும் கனவுகள்!
translated_poem:
On the silver snowy mountain,  
The rays of light awaken,  
In the painting of your eyes,  
I see the dreams I cherish!
